owner_backed_exclusion.obligation_specific_semantic_rationale: Explanation expansion is a client card-surface presentation state; CP-CS may retain the independent managed-access overlay but cannot claim the base interaction state as canonical-service evidence.
Peek availability is decided and rendered by the card action surface; the receiver-managed overlay remains separate and does not convert the base UI affordance into CP-CS evidence.
Peek-open presentation is a local action-surface state, not a canonical-service transition; only the independently required managed-access overlay remains bound.
Hint availability and concealment belong to the card action and interaction contracts; CP-CS cannot claim the base UI state while preserving the independent managed overlay.
Hint reveal is a client interaction state under action-surface and interaction owners; managed entitlement coverage stays an overlay and grants no base CP-CS credit.
Large-text reflow is a platform and PC-Web presentation obligation, so a canonical-service scenario cannot satisfy or mark it not-applicable across checkpoints.
Assistive statistics navigation is owned by platform interaction fidelity and the PC-Web statistics surface, outside CP-CS service execution.
Account overview is a navigational presentation surface; canonical-service evidence may support its data but cannot satisfy the screen obligation.
Membership entry is a product navigation and entitlement-entry surface; CP-CS entitlement reads do not constitute the user-facing entry evidence.
Help is a navigation surface with no canonical-service transaction required by its owner contract.
Privacy is a navigation surface and disclosure experience; it cannot be evidenced by CP-CS service responses.
Sign-out confirmation is the client confirmation boundary preceding session mutation; CP-CS account lifecycle evidence does not satisfy that presentation state.
Delete-account confirmation is the client confirmation boundary preceding destructive account mutation; service execution cannot replace the confirmation evidence.
Accessibility text multiplied by four-choice is an interaction/platform matrix obligation, not a canonical-service scenario outcome.
Motion and input multiplied by interaction family is a client interaction/platform matrix obligation and cannot receive CP-CS coverage.
PC-Web parity is a cross-row web matrix AND obligation; it must be evaluated in CP-WEB and is not a CP-CS not-applicable claim.
